mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.0% indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates for equity valuation, reducing present values and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate below 4.5% signals tightening labor market conditions that accelerate inflationary pressures, prompting Federal Reserve rate hikes and reducing equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE < 4.5%, or Rank IC between UNRATE and 5-day returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Joint growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (HOUST * RSAFS) has Rank IC below 0.05 with 60-day SPX returns over any 3-year rolling window, or average 60-day return when both series are above 50th percentile is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening economic activity that reduces corporate earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods (UNRATE < 5.0% and FEDFUNDS > 3.5%), INDPRO declines are not associated with negative 20-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.05 or t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index above 210.0 indicates elevated inflation that increases monetary tightening risk, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 210.0, or Rank IC between CPIAUCSL and 5-day returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC between GDPC1 growth rate and 60-day SPX returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window, or average 60-day return when GDPC1 growth is in top 25% is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Joint growth in employment (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (PAYEMS * UNRATE) has Rank IC below 0.05 with 5-day SPX returns over any 3-year rolling window, or average 5-day return when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a high interest rate environment (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), a decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, a decline in FEDFUNDS is not associated with positive 60-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.05 or t-test p > 0.05).
